accuracy.reason: All eight objectives remain accurate under stated reverse-proxy and database-effect assumptions; health checks, affinity, draining, retries and redundancy have explicit limits. Diagrams show no automatic transfer of unfinished work.

evidence.quote: Some balancers send traffic to unhealthy targets when every target fails its checks, rather than refusing all traffic.

mechanisms.reason: The lesson explains request/connection selection, count-based policies, sampled readiness, memory location, draining and atomic replay protection with enough state detail for learner transfer.

evidence.quote: Stopping new L4 connections does not stop new HTTP requests on existing connections.

coherence.reason: Proxy flow precedes routing unit and policy; readiness and state establish failure limits before draining, retries and whole-path capacity. Each mechanism supports the next decision.

evidence.quote: Choose the routing unit and required HTTP visibility before choosing a balancing policy.

decisions.reason: Conditional policy choices weigh work/capacity signals; affinity/shared-state costs, rejection under overload and no-balancer option complete the adoption and failure decisions.

evidence.quote: Otherwise redirecting traffic can overload them. Limit or reject excess work visibly instead of assuming redistribution solves it.

clarity.reason: Terms are explained at use, concise examples distinguish requests from work and routing from state durability; no decorative recurring scenario obscures the causal progression.

evidence.quote: Equal turns do not mean equal work

outcomes.reason: Cards 1/2 support proxy return flow, L7 decrypted path routing, L4 reused-connection behavior and omitting unnecessary distribution. Learner covers each.

Cards 3/8 support turns/connections/weights with unequal-work caveats, conditional choices and measurement, unchanged database bottleneck, reachable alternate entry and surviving headroom. Learner covers all criteria.

Card 4 supports useful readiness versus health endpoint, interval/coverage limits, removal only after detection and inability to rescue/replay in-flight work. Learner also preserves all-unhealthy caveat.

Card 5 supports A-only memory loss, affinity placement/load cost without copying, and shared storage access/dependency cost. Learner transfers to cart scenario without claiming durability from routing.

Card 6 teaches stop assignments then bounded completion/shutdown, interruption at deadline, L4 existing-connection management and L7 accepted-work tracking. Learner correctly leaves the unspecified deadline outcome unknown.

Card 7 teaches unknown commit outcome, stable shared durable key/result, atomic effect coordination, failure of new/A-only keys and delayed bounded retries without guaranteed success. Learner covers every criterion.

sourceChecks.claim: AWS ELB describes distribution among targets; reverse-proxy request/response example is correctly scoped and no availability guarantee is inferred.
Microsoft distinguishes transport/network L4 and HTTP-aware L7; inspecting encrypted paths requires TLS termination and separate backend encryption policy.
NGINX documents round robin, least active connections and weighted distribution. Limits from unequal request/connection work justify the lesson conditional choices.
AWS health-check page specifies periodic probes, thresholds and all-unhealthy fail-open; sampling cannot promise future request health or recover in-flight work.
Microsoft web-farm guidance identifies local state consistency and affinity/shared-storage choices; stickiness does not replicate memory or survive loss of its only copy.

AWS deregistration delay stops new requests while allowing in-flight completion; early termination can error. Distinguishing L4 existing connections from L7 requests correctly limits the generic drain plan.
AWS idempotency article verifies stable caller request IDs, shared recognition and ACID token/effect recording; separate non-atomic writes leave the described crash gap.
Google SRE overload guidance supports finite capacity, rejecting excess and preventing cascading retry load; serving-path failover and shared bottlenecks require independent verification.
